essence: A border city between two deserts that each traveller reads as the vessel of escape from his own: across the sand the camel driver sees a ship, out of the sea haze the sailor sees a camel.
textDetails: There are two ways to reach Despina, by sea or by camel, and it presents a different face to each kind of arrival.
The camel driver, on the plateau, sees skyscraper pinnacles, radar antennae, flapping white and red windsocks and smoking chimneys rise over the horizon.
He knows it is a city but imagines it as a ship to take him out of the desert: a sailing ship about to cast off, wind already filling sails that are still tied.
Or a steamer with its boiler throbbing in an iron hull.
He dreams of ports, of foreign cargo swung onto the docks by cranes, of taverns where crews under different flags smash bottles over each other's heads.
And of lamplit street-level windows, in each of which a woman sits combing her hair.
Through the coastal haze the sailor makes out the shape of a camel: a hump (Weaver: withers), two dappled humps with an embroidered, glitter-fringed saddle between them, rocking forward.
He knows it is a city but imagines it as a camel whose pack carries wineskins and bags of candied fruit, date wine and tobacco leaves.
He sees himself leading a long caravan away from the desert of the sea.
His goal: freshwater oases in the jagged shade of palm trees.
And palaces with thick whitewashed walls and tiled courtyards where barefoot dancers move their arms partly within, partly outside their veils.
Marco's conclusion: a city's shape is given by the desert it faces and opposes.
Thus both travellers see Despina as a frontier city set between two deserts.
visualConcept: The diorama is cut in two by a coastline: to the west a golden desert of rippled dunes rising to a tableland, to the east a sea of long blue swells, both running to the horizon and drawn with matching parallel crests so that sand and water read as twin deserts facing each other across the city. Despina is a long strip on the shore, built as one ensemble with two faces. Its landward side is a hull-shaped podium carrying a single fore-and-aft row of seven slender skyscrapers whose needle pinnacles stand like masts, with radar antennae turning at their tops, skybridges like yards hung with rolled awnings that swell like furled sails, red-and-white windsocks streaming like pennants, and four banded chimneys trailing smoke like a steamer's funnels. Its seaward side rises in two great dappled domes, the humps, with a terraced bazaar between them under embroidered canopies, edged by hanging strings of brass lamps and sequins that glitter like a saddle fringe, and a long curved causeway with a lighthouse at its tip for neck and head (domes, bazaar and lighthouse are interpretive translations of what the sailor discerns). Each traveller's desire is made visible as a mirage: seen from the desert, a translucent ghost windjammer locks onto the towers with its sails straining against their ties while far-off ports shimmer above the sea horizon (cranes, taverns, lamplit street-level windows with a woman combing her hair in each); seen from the sea, a ghost camel settles over the domes and sways, and a mirage caravan files across the dunes toward jagged palms, oasis water and thick-walled whitewashed palaces. The ghosts appear only according to where the viewer stands, so the city is a ship or a camel depending on which desert you come from.
layout: The coast runs north-south along x = 0 with a gentle S-curve; land (x < 0) and sea (x > 0) both extend to the fog horizon: a sea plane with Gerstner-style swells, and dunes as a displaced plane with a ripple normal map rising to a tableland edge 2.5 high at x ~ -18, where the camel driver and his camel stand at 0.25-unit human scale. City strip: z from -14 to 14, x from -8 to 6. Landward hull podium 28 long, 4.5 wide, 2.4 high, prow to the north, a row of warm lit windows at ground level; on it seven towers in one line along z (heights bow to stern 11, 15, 18, 17, 14, 12, 9; tapering shafts 1.2-1.6 square plus needle pinnacles of 2-3), radar bars or dishes rotating on four of them, three levels of skybridges between neighbouring towers carrying rolled-awning 'furled sails', 12 red-and-white windsocks on outriggers, four chimneys 8-9 high with red-and-white bands. Seaward: two dome clusters centred near (2, 0, -6) and (2, 0, 5), each a heap of whitewashed cubic houses stepping up to a dome of radius 4.5 that peaks at 6.5, dappled with ochre and terracotta blotches and dark window dots; between them at z ~ 0 a lower saddle bazaar about 6 x 5 of terraces under patterned canopies in carmine, saffron and indigo, with ~200 tiny hanging lamps and mirror sequins along its seaward edge; a curved causeway 10 long from the north dome to a lighthouse 5 high, a short jetty to the south; quays and a few small boats. Ghost ship: a windjammer ~30 long with masts aligned to the towers. Ghost camel: ~28 long, humps aligned to the domes, head over the lighthouse. Mirage strips float at distance 60-90 just above the horizon on the side opposite the viewer.
signatureMotion: 1) Living skyline: windsocks flap, radar antennae turn, smoke streams seaward from the chimneys, the awning-sails breathe as if wind were filling them, the fringe lamps twinkle, and swells roll in from the east while sand drifts in from the west in mirrored rhythm. 2) The traveller's projection: from the land the ghost ship's sails swell and strain and its hull trembles with a faint boiler vibration; from the sea the ghost camel rocks in a slow two-beat stride while the whole silhouette sways in heat-haze distortion. 3) Crossing the border: on toggle the camera arcs high over the city in about 8 seconds; at the top of the arc, between the deserts, both ghosts fade and Despina is briefly only a city.
interactionDescription: Switches which traveller you are. By camel (default): the camera stands on the desert tableland in late gold light, the towers line up as a ship, and the ghost windjammer plus the cranes, taverns and lit windows of imagined ports shimmer over the sea. By ship: the camera crosses to a low point on the water, the domes become two dappled humps under a glittering saddle in the haze, the ghost camel sways and a mirage caravan leads toward palms and whitewashed courts. Ghost opacity follows camera azimuth, so free orbiting reveals the change too.
mood: Late afternoon in great heat, the sun low in the west over the desert. From the land the city is frontlit amber against a pale sea-sky, crisp and gleaming; from the sea it is a backlit silhouette in thick peach haze, rimmed with glitter and trembling with heat shimmer. The air is full of suspended dust and salt, shadows are long and soft, and both shores carry the same mood of imminent departure.
caption: Despina stands on the seam of two deserts, one of sand and one of salt water. From the plateau the camel driver sees towers, radar masts, red and white windsocks and smoking chimneys, and longs for a ship to carry him away. From the coastal haze the sailor sees two dappled humps and a fringed saddle swaying, and longs for a caravan bound for palm shade and whitewashed courts. Each man reads in one skyline the vessel of his own escape.
motto: To the sand it is a ship; to the sea, a camel.
camera: By camel (default): on the tableland west of the city at about (-40, 5.5, 8), target (0, 6, 0), distance ~41, elevation ~2-5 degrees, FOV ~38; the tower row spans the middle third of the frame broadside like a ship, dunes and the driver's camel (head and pack, seen from behind) in the near foreground, a bright sliver of sea beyond. By ship: low on the water at about (38, 1.8, -6), target (0, 5, 0), elevation ~2-6 degrees, a bowsprit tip in the lower corner, the two domes and the fringe silhouetted against the low sun, the tableland faint behind. Gentle orbit allowed; ghosts cross-fade with azimuth.
